summary: Add `meal feedback <deliveryId>` and `meal feedback list [--delivery <id>]` — reports a problem with a delivered meal to Forkable via whichever of two real, undocumented mechanisms actually handles the category: `addMemberReportedIssue` (a real GraphQL mutation for missing-item/missing-side, with refund/credit resolution tracking and a same-day cutoff) or `POST /submit_contact_form` (a REST 'Contact Support' endpoint for everything else). Extends needsCSRF in internal/client/forkable_csrf.go to cover the REST route.
reason: Forkable's my-account SPA exposes exactly four GraphQL account-mutating operations (replacePiece, replaceAllPieces, confirmDelivery, removeDelivery(-ies)); none represent reporting a problem with a delivered meal. The top-level `feedback` command is explicitly CLI-tool-friction-only and never reaches Forkable. Static analysis of the my-account SPA bundle found TWO real, separate submission paths the product's own UI uses for this: (1) module 372's MealReportIssue component calls a real GraphQL mutation, addMemberReportedIssue(input: AddMemberReportedIssueInput!) -- confirmed live via schema-validation probes (orderId: Int, pieceId: String, type: String! required) -- backing a per-meal 'Report Missing Item' widget tied to the courier's Onfleet delivery photos, with a myReportedIssues read field and a server-enforced same-day cutoff (delivery.reportMissingItemCutoff, confirmed live as 1pm local restaurant time; a same-day submission after it is rejected with a payload-level error, not a schema error). (2) module 29822's getSubjectOptions()/submitContactForm() posts to https://forkable.com/submit_contact_form with {name, email, subject, message, market_id} -- the SPA's own copy for 'Other Issues' says outright 'please use Forkable Support', confirming this is the intended fallback for anything the dedicated flow doesn't cover. --category picks the mechanism: missing-item/missing-side -> addMemberReportedIssue (auto-resolves orderId from --piece; --request-refund/--request-credit map to requestRefund/requestGiftCard; blocked with a clear message once the cutoff has passed, checked proactively to avoid a doomed live call); wrong-item/quality/late/other -> the contact form (subjects Report Issue/Report Issue/Delivery Status/General Inquiry; name/email resolved via a live `me` query, market_id via a live myDeliveries lookup, best-effort). Dry-run by default and --confirm-gated like the four GraphQL mutations, reusing buildMutation/mutateGraphQL/confirmOrPreview/emitDryRunShortCircuit for the mutation path. Every attempt is appended to a local meal-feedback.jsonl ledger; `meal feedback list --delivery <id>` additionally exposes Forkable's own myReportedIssues live, for real ground truth on resolution status. Not registered as an MCP tool, matching the existing precedent that feedback and all four meal write commands are excluded from the public MCP tool set.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test clean (4 pre-existing, unrelated internal/cliutil credentials_test.go failures, and the pre-existing phase5/govulncheck findings from stale version-ledger drift and a Go 1.26.5-vs-1.26.6 stdlib CVE gap, all confirmed present on a clean upstream/main checkout before this patch). Dogfooded live end to end against the real account for both mechanisms: (1) addMemberReportedIssue preview correctly auto-resolved the order id from --piece; a --confirm attempt after the real cutoff was correctly rejected server-side, then correctly pre-empted by the proactive cutoff check on a second attempt, with zero myReportedIssues created (verified via 'meal feedback list --delivery <id>' live). (2) the contact-form path returned submitted:true (real HTTP 2xx) for a --category quality follow-up carrying corrected wording, and round-tripped through 'meal feedback list --agent' (local ledger). Usage errors (missing --note on contact-form categories, missing --piece on reported-issue categories, invalid --category) correctly exit 2. Greptile review (PR #1846) found two issues, both addressed: (P2, valid) note truncation could split a multibyte UTF-8 character at the 4096-byte boundary -- extracted a testable truncateValidUTF8 helper using strings.ToValidUTF8, with a new UTF-8-boundary regression test; (P1, valid but a docs bug not a behavior bug) file/help comments claimed 'every attempt (submitted or previewed)' is logged, but a preview-only run intentionally makes no live-writing attempt and is correctly not logged -- corrected the wording to 'every --confirm attempt (submitted or rejected)' rather than changing behavior to log inert previews.
